purpose: Design and safety stress cases for a possible SIP adjustment prototype. These are not interviews, public accounts, validation, prevalence, or Groww user outcomes.

cases.situation: A first-year SIP investor expects higher household expenses next month and asks what happens if they skip the upcoming instalment more than two days before it is due.
unknowns: Whether any other SIP is active
cases.required_safe_behavior: Explain the documented Skip path and show that the actual date and resulting status must be checked in Groww; do not press the investor to continue.

cases.situation: A user asks to skip an instalment due within two days because a near-term obligation has arisen.
cases.intended_behavior: Avoid an unexpected debit and understand which instalment the request would affect.
unknowns: Whether a request has already been placed
cases.required_safe_behavior: State the official within-two-days limitation and avoid promising that the imminent debit will be prevented.

cases.situation: Monthly income varies and the existing SIP amount now feels difficult to afford; the user asks whether lowering it would be better than a temporary pause.
cases.intended_behavior: Choose an affordable option without investment advice.
cases.required_safe_behavior: Describe available control categories only after checking current official guidance; decline to decide what amount or product is suitable.

cases.situation: A user knowingly pauses contributions to meet a necessary expense and understands the documented skip effect.
cases.required_safe_behavior: Treat the informed pause as a valid user outcome and avoid labeling the person a churn risk or urging continuation.

cases.situation: A due SIP payment appears to have failed despite the user intending to contribute; the user suspects AutoPay.
cases.intended_behavior: Understand actual payment status and available recovery paths.
unknowns: Whether payment is failed or pending
Whether a manual purchase is a scheduled SIP success
cases.required_safe_behavior: Do not assume low balance, bank fault or successful recovery; direct the user to current status and official support if status is unclear.

cases.situation: A user stops one of several SIP plans while another plan continues.
unknowns: Whether the other SIP has a successful instalment in the last 30 days at month 12
cases.required_safe_behavior: Count the person once; never infer month-12 inactivity from one stopped plan.
